answer: Yes. The transition handler in srv/order-service.js registers submit with from = 'O' and rejects with 409 when the stored status_code is not 'O', so the UI promise is enforced on the server; the check is table-driven, which is why the static parser saw a computed value.

findings.title: Orders.submit enforces status_code = O via the TRANSITIONS table
findings.statement: The handler loops over TRANSITIONS and registers this.on(action, Orders, ...) for each; for submit, from = 'O', so a stored status other than 'O' is rejected with 409 before the UPDATE to 'S'. This matches the @Core.OperationAvailable rule. The table-driven pattern (action, from, to) is a candidate for a deterministic rule.

evidence.quote: for (const [action, from, to] of TRANSITIONS) this.on(action, Orders, async req => {
if (from && order.status_code !== from) return req.reject(409, `Only orders in status ${from} can do this`)
